title: Endometrial Hyperplasia, EIN & Lynch Syndrome Genetics
subject: ss-gynaecological-oncology
refs: SGO Clinical Practice Statement: Screening for Lynch Syndrome in Endometrial Cancer

steps.say: Endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia represents the clonal precursor lesion to endometrioid carcinoma. Morphological diagnosis hinges on gland crowding where crowded glandular elements outstrip surrounding stroma.
steps.tx: Monoclonal premalignant transformation is designated as **EIN** (**atypical hyperplasia**). Histopathological criteria require glandular crowding with **volume percent stroma <55%** (glands exceeding stroma), cytological demarcation, and lesion size >1 mm. Significantly, immediate surgical hysterectomy reveals an underlying **40-45% concurrent adenocarcinoma** in **40** to **45** percent of cases.

steps.say: Surgical extirpation represents the definitive standard of care for atypical lesions once childbearing is complete. Total hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy should strictly avoid morcellation techniques.
steps.tx: For postmenopausal women or patients who have finished childbearing, **definitive management** of atypical hyperplasia is total hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (**TH-BSO**). Minimally invasive removal must ensure specimen integrity with strict **avoidance of morcellation** to prevent iatrogenic intraperitoneal dissemination of occult invasive carcinoma.

rows: Strict avoidance of power morcellation dissemination

steps.say: Young women desiring childbearing may pursue conservative hormonal management under stringent surveillance. Intrauterine levonorgestrel delivery or high dose oral progestins achieve high pathological regression rates.
steps.tx: Young patients desiring **fertility preservation** may undergo medical progestin therapy utilizing the **LNG-IUD 52 mg** (levonorgestrel intrauterine system) or oral **megestrol acetate 160 mg** daily. This approach achieves an objective histological **regression rate 80-90%** (**80** to **90** percent) typically within **6** to **9** months of therapy.

left.title: Levonorgestrel IUD (52 mg LNG-IUD)
points: Minimal systemic metabolic and thromboembolic side effects
Higher patient compliance and durability for 5 years

right.title: High-Dose Oral Megestrol Acetate (160 mg daily)
points: Weight gain, fluid retention, and thromboembolic risk
Combined option for incomplete response to local IUD

steps.say: Close histological monitoring during medical progestin therapy is vital to detect persistent or progressive lesions. Endometrial sampling must be performed at quarterly to semi annual intervals.
steps.tx: Endometrial surveillance mandates **endometrial biopsy every 3-6 months** (**3** to **6** months) along with direct **hysteroscopic evaluation**. Continued conservative management requires documenting **2** **consecutive negative specimens** before attempting assisted conception, with definitive hysterectomy recommended immediately after completion of desired childbearing.

nodes.label: Initiate LNG-IUD 52 mg or megestrol acetate 160 mg
Perform endometrial biopsy every 3-6 months with hysteroscopy
Document 2 consecutive negative biopsies 3 months apart
Expedite assisted conception or perform definitive TH-BSO

steps.say: Hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer represents the most prevalent familial cause of endometrial malignancies. Germline DNA mismatch repair defects confer high lifetime endometrial cancer risks.
steps.tx: **Lynch syndrome** arises from autosomal dominant germline mutations in **MMR genes MLH1 MSH2 MSH6 PMS2** (or EPCAM deletions). Mutation carriers face a **40-60% lifetime endometrial cancer risk** (**40** to **60** percent), which frequently functions as the primary **sentinel cancer** presenting years prior to colorectal adenocarcinoma in over half of affected women.

steps.say: Current clinical consensus mandates routine testing of all endometrial malignancies for mismatch repair proficiency. Reflex immunohistochemistry and microsatellite instability assays identify inherited cases.
steps.tx: International societies establish a **universal screening** protocol (**SGO/NCCN recommendation**) mandating **MMR immunohistochemistry** (testing MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, and PMS2 protein expression) or **MSI testing** on all newly resected endometrial carcinoma specimens, regardless of patient age or family pedigree, to identify prospective Lynch syndrome kindreds.

nodes.label: Diagnose endometrial adenocarcinoma on surgical pathology
Perform universal MMR immunohistochemistry on all tumors
Intact MMR proteins: mismatch repair proficient (pMMR)
Loss of MSH2, MSH6, or PMS2: refer for germline genetic testing

steps.say: When immunohistochemistry reveals dual loss of MLH1 and PMS2, epigenetic silencing must be distinguished from inherited mutations. Somatic promoter hypermethylation accounts for the vast majority of cases.
steps.tx: Loss of MLH1 and PMS2 expression triggers reflex **MLH1 promoter hypermethylation** analysis. Epigenetic promoter methylation accounts for **sporadic epigenetic silencing** in over **90** percent of cases (not heritable), whereas unmethylated tumors (**10** percent) represent genuine germline mutations requiring genetic sequencing for **germline differentiation** and family cascade testing.

left.title: Sporadic MLH1 Hypermethylation (~90%)
points: No germline mutation; family cascade testing not required

right.title: Germline MLH1 Mutation (Lynch Syndrome ~10%)
points: Inherited autosomal dominant pathogenic germline variant
Requires genetic counseling and full family cascade screening

steps.say: Prophylactic surgical extirpation eliminates the risk of future endometrial and ovarian malignancies in mutation carriers. The timing of surgery is tailored to the specific mismatch repair gene.
steps.tx: In confirmed carriers, **risk-reducing hysterectomy** with **prophylactic BSO** is recommended between **age 35-40** (**35** to **40** years) for MLH1 and MSH2 carriers after childbearing. In **MSH6/PMS2 carriers**, risk accrues later, permitting deferral of prophylactic surgery until age **45** years, completely mitigating gynecological cancer mortality.
